meta.pipeline: pipeline/analyze_customer_files.py (pre-computed; simulates the future Marigold ingestion pipeline)
meta.disclaimer: Demo analysis on fictional data. Not tax advice.

eligibility.headline: Volterra appears to qualify, but eligibility cannot yet be fully established
eligibility.summary: 4 of 7 requirements are satisfied by the files provided. 3 need more information or review.

requirements.title: Products are battery cells that meet the technical definition
requirements.explanation: Each cell must store at least 12 Wh, hold at least 100 Wh per liter, stay within a 100:1 capacity-to-power ratio, and have its capacity measured under a recognized standard.
requirements.fact: Every tested product clears the thresholds by a wide margin: VX-2170 rev B: 18.0 Wh, 742 Wh/L, capacity-to-power 0.25:1; VX-LFP50 rev A: 155.5 Wh, 385 Wh/L, capacity-to-power 0.97:1 (draft report). Some test evidence is missing or unapproved.
requirements.next_action: Approve the VX-LFP50 test report and obtain test evidence for VX-2170 revision C.

requirements.title: Volterra makes the cells itself
requirements.explanation: The claimant must do the manufacturing that turns materials into a finished cell, not just minor assembly.
requirements.fact: Volterra makes its own cathode and anode electrodes from purchased materials and assembles the cells itself (15 production orders in 2026, all at its own plant).

requirements.title: Cells are made in the United States
requirements.explanation: Cells must be produced in the U.S. Using imported materials is allowed.
requirements.fact: All 15 production orders ran at Volterra Holland Cell Plant, 4100 Lakeshore Industrial Drive, Holland, MI 49423.

requirements.title: Cells were sold in 2026 to unrelated customers
requirements.explanation: Only cells sold during the tax year count, and buyers must not be under common control with Volterra.
requirements.fact: 23 invoices in 2026 to 3 customers. Company records list no parent or affiliates. 2 January 2027 invoices are outside the tax year and excluded.

requirements.title: Volterra is not a restricted foreign entity
requirements.explanation: The company claiming the credit cannot itself be a foreign entity of concern or controlled by one.
requirements.fact: Volterra Battery Systems, Inc. is a Delaware C corporation with no parent company listed.

requirements.title: Materials do not come from restricted foreign sources
requirements.explanation: For 2026, a cell does not qualify if too much of its material is traced to prohibited foreign entities.
requirements.fact: This test has not been performed. The method is not in the documents available, and ownership or attestation evidence is incomplete for: Eastbay Separator Co., Ltd., Nordvik Electrolyte AB.
requirements.next_action: Close the supplier evidence gaps, then have a tax advisor perform the sourcing test.

requirements.title: No overlapping §48C investment credit
requirements.explanation: Equipment that already earned a §48C investment credit cannot also be used to earn 45X credit.
requirements.fact: The company records do not address §48C.
requirements.next_action: Confirm no §48C credit was taken for the Holland plant.

credit_summary.basis: Cells sold to unrelated customers in 2026 x tested capacity (kWh) x $35 per kWh. Where capacity is disputed, the lower value is used.

steps.label: Capacity per cell (from the capacity test)

credit_calculations.note: Later revisions have no capacity test of their own. The tested capacity of revision B is applied to all cells sold, pending that test.
credit_calculations.plain: Volterra sold 46,500 VX-2170 cells in 2026. Each stores 18.00 Wh, so together they hold 837 kWh. Section 45X pays $35 per kWh, which gives about $29,295.

steps.label: Capacity per cell (from the capacity test)

credit_calculations.note: Product record and test report disagree (160.00 Wh vs 155.52 Wh). The estimate uses the lower value; with the higher value it would be $56,000.
credit_calculations.plain: Volterra sold 10,000 VX-LFP50 cells in 2026. Each stores 155.52 Wh, so together they hold 1,555 kWh. Section 45X pays $35 per kWh, which gives about $54,432.

products.name: VX-2170 Cylindrical NMC Cell

revisions.change: Separator changed from SEP-016 (16 um) to SEP-021 (12 um ceramic-coated) for cost reduction.

revision_changes: From July 1, 2026, revision C switches the separator from Tamarack Membrane Inc. (16 µm, made in United States) to Eastbay Separator Co., Ltd. (12 µm, ceramic-coated, made in Malaysia).

issues.title: Foreign-entity sourcing test has not been performed
issues.description: For 2026, a cell does not qualify if it includes 'material assistance' from a prohibited foreign entity. The documents available to Marigold state this restriction but not the method for testing it, and supplier evidence is incomplete for 2 supplier(s).
issues.why: If the test fails for a product, none of that product's cells qualify.
issues.next_action: Have a tax advisor apply current IRS guidance on material assistance using the bill of materials, material costs and supplier documents already provided, after the supplier gaps below are closed.

issues.title: Nordvik Electrolyte AB: supplier attestation expired
issues.description: The attestation on file covers deliveries through 2026-06-30. 10 material deliveries received 2026-07-01 to 2026-11-26 are not covered, and they were used in 10 production lots.
issues.why: Without a current attestation, the supplier's representations do not cover material used in these lots.
issues.next_action: Obtain a renewed attestation from Nordvik Electrolyte AB covering deliveries from 2026-06-30 onward.

issues.title: VX-LFP50 capacity is not settled
issues.description: The product record lists 50.0 Ah (160.0 Wh), while the test report shows 48.6 Ah (155.52 Wh). The test report is an unapproved draft.
issues.why: Capacity drives the credit. The two values give $54,432 and $56,000; Marigold uses the lower value until this is resolved.
issues.next_action: Have engineering confirm the rated capacity and approve (sign) the test report, then update the product record if needed.

issues.title: No capacity test for VX-2170 revision C
issues.description: Testing on file covers revision B only. Revision C became effective 2026-07-01 (Separator changed from SEP-016 (16 um) to SEP-021 (12 um ceramic-coated) for cost reduction.). No evidence shows whether the earlier test still applies.
issues.why: Capacity must be measured under a recognized standard. It sets both whether the cell qualifies and how much credit it earns.
issues.next_action: Obtain a capacity test report for VX-2170 revision C, or an engineering assessment that revision C does not change the tested capacity.

issues.title: Eastbay Separator Co., Ltd.: ultimate parent unresolved
issues.description: Eastbay Separator Co., Ltd. identifies its immediate parent (Eastbay Holdings Pte. Ltd. (Singapore) - 100%) but states its ultimate parent is 'Not disclosed - confidential'. No other customer file identifies the ultimate owner.
issues.why: Ownership is needed to judge whether this supplier is a restricted foreign entity for the sourcing test.
issues.next_action: Request a full ownership disclosure from Eastbay Separator Co., Ltd., identifying every owner above the immediate parent.

issues.title: §48C status of the Holland plant not documented
issues.description: Nothing in the company records says whether any equipment at the plant received a §48C investment credit after August 16, 2022.
issues.why: Cells made with such equipment cannot also earn 45X credit. The answer is usually a quick confirmation.
issues.next_action: Confirm in writing that no property at the Holland plant received a §48C credit after August 16, 2022.

issues.title: Unidentified product on invoice 90041233
issues.description: 140 units of 'VXLFP50 CELL B-GRADE' (material MAT-10004759) were sold to Circuit Loop Recycling LLC on 11/24/2026. That material number does not match either product, and no production lot is recorded.
issues.why: The sale cannot be tied to a qualifying product or lot, so it is left out of the estimate.
issues.next_action: Identify what was sold and which lot it came from. If they were eligible cells, add the lot reference so they can be evaluated.

issues.title: Production count mismatch on lot V21260706
issues.description: The production order reports 6,212 good cells, but the lot record shows 6,150 (a difference of 62). Material usage matches the lower figure.
issues.why: Production counts support how many cells were available to sell. Sales do not exceed the lower figure, so the estimate is unaffected.
issues.next_action: Ask the plant to correct the production order or explain the difference.

tax_rules.title: Who can claim the credit
tax_rules.plain: The credit is for eligible components that the company produced in the United States and sold during the tax year, in its business, to unrelated buyers.
tax_rules.quote: Form 7207 is used to claim the advanced manufacturing production credit under section 45X for eligible components produced by the taxpayer within the United States (including U.S. territories) and sold during the tax year in the taxpayer's trade or business to unrelated persons.

tax_rules.document: T.D. 10010, Advanced Manufacturing Production Credit, Final Rule (89 FR 85798)
tax_rules.title: What counts as a battery cell
tax_rules.plain: A battery cell must have positive and negative electrodes, store at least 12 watt-hours, and hold at least 100 watt-hours per liter of volume.
tax_rules.quote: Battery cell means an electrochemical cell- (A) Comprised of one or more positive electrodes and one or more negative electrodes; (B) With a volumetric energy density of not less than 100 watt-hours per liter; and (C) Capable of storing at least 12 watt-hours of energy.

tax_rules.document: T.D. 10010, Advanced Manufacturing Production Credit, Final Rule (89 FR 85798)
tax_rules.title: How capacity must be measured
tax_rules.plain: A cell's capacity must be measured using a recognized national or international test standard.
tax_rules.quote: Taxpayers must measure the capacity of a battery cell in accordance with a national or international standard, such as IEC 60086-1 (Primary Batteries), or an equivalent standard.

tax_rules.document: T.D. 10010, Advanced Manufacturing Production Credit, Final Rule (89 FR 85798)
tax_rules.title: Credit amount for battery cells
tax_rules.plain: The credit is $35 for each kilowatt-hour of battery-cell capacity.
tax_rules.quote: For a battery cell, the credit amount is equal to the product of $35 multiplied by the capacity of such battery cell, subject to the limitation provided in paragraph (e)(5) of this section. The capacity of a battery cell is expressed on a kilowatt-hour basis.

tax_rules.title: Total capacity = cells x capacity per cell
tax_rules.plain: Total qualifying capacity is the number of cells produced and sold multiplied by the capacity of each cell in kilowatt-hours.
tax_rules.quote: The aggregate capacity of eligible battery components is determined by multiplying the number of eligible components produced and sold by the capacity of each component expressed on a kilowatt-hour basis.

tax_rules.document: T.D. 10010, Advanced Manufacturing Production Credit, Final Rule (89 FR 85798)
tax_rules.title: Capacity-to-power limit
tax_rules.plain: A cell's capacity divided by its maximum discharge power cannot exceed 100 to 1. Cells built for very slow discharge do not qualify.
tax_rules.quote: ...a battery cell or battery module must not exceed a capacity-to-power ratio of 100:1. ... capacity-to-power ratio means, with respect to a battery cell or battery module, the ratio of the capacity of such cell or module to the maximum discharge amount of such cell or module.

tax_rules.document: T.D. 10010, Advanced Manufacturing Production Credit, Final Rule (89 FR 85798)
tax_rules.section: § 1.45X-1(c)(1) Definition of produced by the taxpayer
tax_rules.title: The company must do the manufacturing
tax_rules.plain: The claimant must itself transform materials into the finished cell, not just do minor assembly.
tax_rules.quote: The term produced by the taxpayer means a process conducted by the taxpayer that substantially transforms constituent elements, materials, or subcomponents into a complete and distinct eligible component that is functionally different from that which would result from minor assembly or superficial modification...

tax_rules.document: T.D. 10010, Advanced Manufacturing Production Credit, Final Rule (89 FR 85798)
tax_rules.title: Made in the United States
tax_rules.plain: The cell must be produced in the United States. Imported materials used to make it are allowed.
tax_rules.quote: ...produced within the United States, as defined in section 638(1) of the Code... (2) Subcomponents. Constituent elements, materials, and subcomponents used in the production of eligible components are not subject to the domestic production requirement...

tax_rules.document: T.D. 10010, Advanced Manufacturing Production Credit, Final Rule (89 FR 85798)
tax_rules.section: § 1.45X-1(e) Production and sale in a trade or business
tax_rules.title: Made and sold in the course of business
tax_rules.plain: Production and sale must be part of the company's regular business.
tax_rules.quote: An eligible component produced and sold by the taxpayer is taken into account for purposes of the section 45X credit only if the production and sale are in a trade or business (within the meaning of section 162 of the Code) of the taxpayer.

tax_rules.title: Sales must be to unrelated buyers
tax_rules.plain: Sales to companies under common control with the seller do not count unless a special election is made.
tax_rules.quote: For purposes of the advanced manufacturing production credit, persons are treated as related to each other if such persons would be treated as a single employer under the regulations prescribed under the common control rules of section 52(b).

tax_rules.section: Special Rules - Material assistance from prohibited foreign entities
tax_rules.title: Supplier / foreign-entity sourcing restriction
tax_rules.plain: For 2026, a cell does not qualify if it includes 'material assistance' from a prohibited foreign entity - broadly, too much of its material cost traced to restricted foreign suppliers.
tax_rules.quote: For tax years beginning after July 4 2025, an "eligible component" doesn't include any property which includes any material assistance from a prohibited foreign entity...
tax_rules.limitation: The repository's documents state this restriction but do not include the method or thresholds for testing it. Marigold therefore does not decide pass/fail; it organizes the cost and supplier evidence for review.

tax_rules.section: Special Rules - Prohibited foreign entity restrictions
tax_rules.title: The company itself must not be a restricted foreign entity
tax_rules.plain: No credit is allowed if the claiming company is a specified foreign entity or foreign-influenced entity.
tax_rules.quote: In general, for tax years beginning after July 4, 2025, no advanced manufacturing production credit will be allowed if the taxpayer is a specified foreign entity, as defined in section 7701(a)(51)(B), or a foreign-influenced entity, as defined in section 7701(a)(51)(D)...

tax_rules.title: No double benefit with the §48C investment credit
tax_rules.plain: Cells made with equipment from a facility that already received a §48C investment credit (after August 16, 2022) cannot also earn 45X credit.
tax_rules.quote: You can't claim the advanced manufacturing production credit for eligible components produced using any property that is part of a facility for which a credit under section 48C was previously taken after August 16, 2022.

tax_rules.title: Full credit for 2026 sales
tax_rules.plain: The credit starts phasing down only for components sold after 2029, so 2026 sales receive 100%.
tax_rules.quote: The credit for advanced manufacturing production will phase out for eligible components sold after 2029, except applicable critical minerals.

tax_rules.title: One computation per facility
tax_rules.plain: The credit is computed separately for each production facility.
tax_rules.quote: File a separate Form 7207 for each facility operated to produce and sell eligible components.
